doc.title: Dave Pell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Reflections on being a leader and closing
summary: Pell says watching leaders made him want to lead and that spreading out is like improvising; Rowe thanks him.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: It’s been fascinating. Man of many hats.

I loved it. I think I would have been happier just playing. But it wasn’t enough for me. It wasn’t enough of a challenge. I figured it’s like sitting there in the band and watching the leader and then realizing all the things he did wrong, and saying I’m going to be the leader now. All right I’m the leader, now what? Well I got 30 albums. Well now what? You know? You keep on wanting to spread out. It’s like improvising. Exactly like improvising. It’s making something happen. So it’s fun. It’s great.
Well on behalf of he college, we would like to thank you for that really marvelous hour of reminiscing and I can’t imagine what the next thing for you is going to be?
Well I’ll tell you — © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
We’ll do Part II in a few years, and we’ll see what else you’re into.
Well on behalf of Hamilton I want to thank you for joining us today, it’s been a real pleasure.
I’ve enjoyed it. I hope I haven’t talked too much.
Beautiful. Thank you. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
